text:
Calm as a sage, meek as one accursed, I said:

I love you, O my beauty, my enchantress…

How many times…

Your thirstless orgies, your soulless loves,
your taste for the infinite
proclaimed in everything, even evil,

Your bombs, your daggers, your victories, your festivals,
your melancholy neighborhoods,
your sumptuous hotels,
your gardens filled with intrigues and sighs,
your temples vomiting musical prayers,
your childish tantrums, your games of a mad old woman,
your despondencies;

Your fireworks, eruptions of joy
that make the dark and silent sky laugh.

Your venerable vice, flaunted in silk,
and your laughable virtue, with its unhappy
and gentle gaze, enraptured by the luxury it displays…

Your rescued principles, your vulnerable laws,
your high monuments where mist hangs,
your metal towers glittering in the sun,
your queens of the stage with enchanting voices,
your alarm bells, your deafening cannon,
your magic paving stones that raise fortresses,

Your paltry orators with baroque manners,
preaching love, and your sewers, brimming with blood,

Sinking into Hell like Orinocos.

Your fools, your angels, new in their tinsel.
Angels clad in gold, hyacinth, and purple,
bear witness that I fulfilled my duty
like a perfect chemist, like a devout soul.

For from each thing I drew its quintessence:—

You gave me your mud and I turned it into gold.

translation.title: Draft Epilogue
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. The draft’s fragmentary opening, catalog of the city, and alchemical close are retained.
